## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a775481935f73fefdfa78ee1724021cc2e4eb56d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json, skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md, skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md + none

First review of this head. Read: card #33868 and its four comments (6894608532, 6896874152, 6897100433, 6897496261), the PR body, the file list (4 files) and the net diff `origin/main...a7754819` (the head is one merge of main `03b4d2d1` over `f1a9233f`; the net diff is +45/-21 in those 4 files). The semantic change taught is PR #33854 (merged as `0ac112fc`, an ancestor of the `origin/main` read here, `bc6b7ffd`); its records 6894395884, 6895214298 and 6896557459 were read for what was promised. No file in the diff implements or enforces the three `hits` files, hence `+ none`. The changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT; its level and declaration lines are judged in ②. Code named below is on `origin/main`, read to judge, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Null or absent column fails the five ordering operators, engine-evaluated positions.** True. `packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts`: `NULL_IS_NOT_ORDERED_OPERATORS = new Set(['$gt', '$gte', '$lt', '$lte', '$between'])`, and in `checkCondition` `if (value === undefined && !NO_VALUE_ANSWERED_BY_OPERATOR.has(op)) return false;` followed by `if (value === null && NULL_IS_NOT_ORDERED_OPERATORS.has(op) && !orderingComparandHoldsNull(op, target)) return false;`. `having-filter-null-ordering.test.ts` pins it on the three faces that share the walker (`matchesAggregationFilter`, `applyHaving`, `matchesDriverWhere`), with `amount` null on one row and absent on another.
- **"in `where` ... alike".** True on every `where` path I could read. SQL `where`: record 6894395884 measured the walker against driver-sql's where compiler, and the five operators were the only divergence on a NULL column. Plugin-driver in-memory `where`: `driver-query-in-memory.ts` filters with `matchesDriverWhere`. driver-memory's own `find`: pinned by `memory-matcher-null-value-and-comparand.test.ts` (#13553, `{ n: { $lte: 0 } }` keeps only the row storing 0; #13549 for a bounded `$between`). The PR body lists this as not measured; the pin exists. driver-mongodb's own `where` has no pin I read; it rests on BSON type bracketing. Nothing in the tree contradicts the sentence.
- **`having` on an empty aggregate.** True. `in-memory-aggregation.ts`: `out[alias] = nums.length === 0 ? null : ...` for `avg`, the same for `min` / `max`, and the comment "count/count_distinct/sum → 0, avg/min/max → null"; the test "an empty group's avg is not ≤ 0" pins `applyHaving` dropping it. `having` is engine-applied on both routes (`return applyHaving(aggregated, ast.having, ...)` on the pushed-down one), so the sentence holds on driver-sql too. Wording: see N1.
- **`null` is not an ordering comparand, refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400.** True at all three positions. `packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts`: `if (ORDERING_COMPARAND_OPERATORS.has(op)) { if (spec[op] === null) { throw nullOrderingComparandError(...) } }`; the engine runs that door on `where` (`engine-top-level.ts`), on each `aggregations[i].filter` and on `having` (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `assertListComparandShapes(object, 'aggregate', aggFilter, ...)` and `(..., query.having, 'having')`). The bare `{ deleted_at: null }` sentence is the old section's rule, kept; the walker test pins `{ amount: null }` selecting the null and the absent row.
- **Unchanged operators.** The skill teaches none of them either way, which is consistent: it does not enumerate `$ne`, `$nin`, `$notContains`, `$exists`, `$null` or the equality family on a no-value column anywhere. `$empty` sits with them in `NO_VALUE_ANSWERED_BY_OPERATOR` and is pinned unmoved. It should not be named alone: naming one member of a set the file does not teach would imply the others differ. The existing `$empty` rows (`IS NULL`, `''` or `[]` by type) already say a null column is empty. No finding; the dev's option A stands.
- **Pushdown only on drivers declaring the bit.** True as to which drivers: `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` reads `const aggregationFilterNative = drv?.supports?.aggregationFilter === true;`; `sql-driver.ts` declares `aggregationFilter: true`; `turso-driver.ts` has `...(this.transportMode === 'remote' ? { aggregationFilter: false } : {})`. "On any other driver the engine reads the scoped rows and evaluates the filter itself" is the `find()` plus `applyInMemoryAggregation` branch, and promises nothing more. The sentence is unqualified about WHEN the declaring driver gets the call; see S1.
- **Answers what `where` answers, text by the database collation.** True when pushed down: `sql-driver-top-level.ts` says the driver "compiles a measure filter with the SAME where compiler (`applyFilters`) a `where` goes through", and the bit's describe text reads "except that text compares by the backend collation as in `where`".
- **Refuses what `where` refuses.** The named case is true and is the pinned one: `aggregation-filter-where-doors.test.ts` row 3 (`{ amount: { $gt: { $field: 'nope' } } }`, 400 `INVALID_FILTER`) and the #33698 re-recorded audit-opt-out case. The dev was right not to write "undeclared column" bare: a plain undeclared key answers `INVALID_FIELD` (row 4).

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right: prose and one eval fixture in the published bundle, no schema, no code. It is the name the neighbouring skills changesets use.
- `Clause-②: no` is right: no accept set moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: the semantic change was declared by #33854 (`semantic`, per S1 of record 6894395884); this PR pays its `Skills-docs: follow-up` and changes no meaning itself. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two lines.
- Check-runs on this head, read at about 2026-11-15T16:21Z: 41 runs, 18 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 7 still running: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Green already: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Build Core`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`. The skill gates (token ratchet, skill-docs, skill-links, skill-examples) had not reported under a finished lint family at read time; the dev's local readings of them are in the report, and the running families are the seat's to wait for before landing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Authoring tier.** The claim (6897100433) and the report record that the card thread is served below the contract-review tier and that authoring and the commit ran in an isolated os-dev subagent pinned to it on the same branch. That is declared before the work and repeated in the PR body. I cannot verify the subagent's served tier from the inputs given; it is the seat's to hold with the transcript. It does not change what the tree says.
- **The two removals in `filters.md`.** (a) The case-sensitivity paragraph: its home is SKILL.md, String Operators, which reads "compare CASE-SENSITIVELY; `$icontains` is the case-INSENSITIVE twin (ASCII folding only). So the user-facing cases want `$icontains`". Both the rule and the advice survive, the pointer left in `filters.md` names the section in the form the file already uses for Logical Operators, and SKILL.md is the entry a reader comes through. Lost with no home: the `café` / `CAFÉ` illustration and the `filter.zod.ts` citation; neither is a rule. (b) The second Date example: `$between` keeps its table row here and its row and example in SKILL.md; a `Date` as a comparand keeps the `$gte: new Date(...)` example directly above. No rule lost. Both removals are genuine deletion of restatement in the same file, which is what the ratchet discipline asks for.
- **`dashboards.md` untouched.** Verified: its one mention is the envelope table row "WHERE (`$and/$or/$not` on the base object) + measure-scoped filters"; it states no evaluation path. Right to leave.
- **Ratchet row.** `filters.md` measures 2473 against a row of 2482 (0 headroom on main). The gate's header says lowering "is always legitimate and encouraged" and its row history re-locks at the measurement; it does not require it. See N3.
- **`aggregation.md`** grows 2096 to 2221 inside its existing row of 2357 with no deletion. The gate accepts it and the headroom is not one of the two reserved rows the header names. Noted, no finding.
- **Open question 1 (`$empty`)**: A, as judged in ①. **Open question 2 (re-lock)**: N3.
- **Out-of-scope note in the report** (whether a pushed-down measure filter answers `$like` / `$ilike`, which `filters.md` says objectql `having` and service-analytics refuse): the sentence in `filters.md` names `having` and service-analytics, not a measure filter, so this diff leaves no contradiction. Not examined further.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

`skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md`. The new section is true (①), sits where the old null advice sat, keeps that advice as its last sentence, and gives the one spelling an author needs. It reads consistently with the rest of the file: "an aggregation's `filter` and `having`" is the phrase the Relation Filters section already uses. The heading changed; nothing in `skills/**` links to the old heading. A grep of `skills/**` for other statements about empty values and ordering filters, the in-memory path, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and a conditional aggregate finds no contradiction left: the only other hits are the `$null` / `$exists` / `$empty` tables, which agree.

`skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md`. The false sentence ("forces the in-memory path, no driver compiles a conditional aggregate") is gone, and what replaces it is true for the call the card describes. One over-statement:

S1 (should-fix): "A driver that declares `supports.aggregationFilter` ... runs it in the database" is not true of every call on such a driver. The route condition is `typeof drv.aggregate === 'function' && allStructuredSupported && !tzRequiresInMemory && (!hasAggregationFilter || aggregationFilterNative)`, with `tzRequiresInMemory = !!tz && tz !== 'UTC' && hasDateBucket`. So on driver-sql an aggregate that buckets a date under a non-UTC `timezone`, or by a granularity the dialect does not bucket, stays on `find()` plus the in-memory path, measure filters included. On that call the sentence "it answers what the same condition answers there (text by the database collation)" is false: the call's `where` goes to the database and the measure filter is compared in JS, so on a case-insensitive collation `stage: 'won'` counts differently in the two positions. A dataset with a date dimension and an organisation time zone is an ordinary shape, not a corner. The same file already teaches the bucketing fallback (Date-Bucketed Grouping: "transparently falls back to in-memory bucketing otherwise"), so the reader has the concept. One clause closes it, for example: "runs it in the database whenever the aggregate itself is pushed down (a date bucket under a non-UTC `timezone`, or one the dialect cannot bucket, keeps the whole call in memory)". The no-value rule is unaffected either way, as the callout's last sentence says. `aggregation.md` has 136 tokens of headroom.

N1 (nit): "`avg` / `min` / `max` over no rows is `null`". The code's condition is no non-null VALUES (the fold keeps only values that are not null, then answers `null` when none is left), which also covers a group whose rows all lack the field, the case a plain `groupBy` actually produces (a group always has a row). "over no values" is truer and no longer. The example alias `average` appears nowhere else in the section; harmless.

`skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json`, case 8. Self-consistent: each of `filter`, `$or`, `$lte: 0` and `$null: true` occurs in `expected_output` (checked by string inclusion on the parsed file); `must_not_contain` is empty, so no correct answer restating the rule can trip it. The prompt matches the card's scenario ("count where amount $lte 0") and `expected_output` is correct against the code: `count` with no `field`, the per-measure `filter`, and the `$or` with `$null: true`. It follows the file's hand formatting.

N2 (nit): the assertions are loose in one direction and strict in the other. `filter` matches any answer that uses the word; `filter:` would bind it to the key. And `$or` / `$null: true` fail two answers the engine also answers correctly: `$empty: true` on the number field, and `{ $not: { amount: { $gt: 0 } } }` (the walker test pins negation keeping the no-value rows). The case tests the taught spelling, which is a fair thing for an eval to do; left as is or tightened in a later pass.

N3 (nit): re-lock the `filters.md` row at 2473. Leaving 9 tokens gives the next author growth that no deletion paid for, on a file that sat at zero; the gate's own history banks a shrink at the measurement. It is a one-line edit to a governed script and has no effect on what the skill teaches, so it does not hold this head; do it in this PR if S1 is taken, or in the next PR that touches the file.

Sibling skills: no other skill states how a measure filter or `having` is evaluated; `objectstack-ui` `dashboards.md` only lists the capability. No contradiction left elsewhere.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d47493babcaa8ba290719aa97dc1a419d3f5e1f4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json, skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md, skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md + scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs

Delta review of record 6897568297, which judged head `a7754819` in full (PASS, with S1 open and nits N1, N2, N3). That record stands as written except where this one says otherwise. Read: the commit range `a7754819..d47493ba`, the net diff against main, the r2 PR body, and the check-runs on this head.

The range is two commits. `b87277b6` (single parent `a7754819`) touches two files, +14/-6: `skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md` and `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. `d47493ba` is a merge of `b87277b6` with main `bc6b7ffd`. Verified: `git diff --name-only b87277b6 d47493ba` lists seven files, all under `scripts/pm/**` or `.claude/**` (three in `scripts/pm/fleet-write`, two in `scripts/pm`, two in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references`), so the dev's statement about the merge holds; and `git diff --name-only bc6b7ffd d47493ba` lists exactly the PR's five files, so the merge brought nothing of its own into the net diff. `filters.md`, the eval file and the changeset are byte-identical to the head the earlier record judged. The net diff is now 5 files, +54/-22.

Closures, by id:

- S1: closed.
- N1: closed.
- N3: closed.
- N2: left as is by the dev (stated in the PR body); it was a nit and stays one.

No new must-fix or should-fix. One new nit, N4.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1, the pushdown clause.** The callout now reads that a declaring driver "runs it in the database whenever the aggregate itself is pushed down (a date bucket under a non-UTC `timezone`, or one the driver does not bucket natively, keeps the whole call in memory)". Checked against `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` on this head. The first exception is `const tzRequiresInMemory = !!tz && tz !== 'UTC' && hasDateBucket;`. The second is `const granularityCaps = drv?.supports?.queryDateGranularity;` and `allStructuredSupported`, which is `structuredItems.every(...)` returning `granularityCaps?.[g.dateGranularity] === true` for each item that carries a `dateGranularity`. Both sit in the one route condition beside `(!hasAggregationFilter || aggregationFilterNative)`, and when either fails the call takes `driver.find()` plus `applyInMemoryAggregation`, measure filters included. The dev's "the driver does not bucket natively" is the more exact reading than my suggested "the dialect cannot bucket": the engine reads a per-granularity bit the DRIVER advertises, and the code's own comment names a driver face that advertises none (the Turso remote transport). "One" reads back to "a date bucket", which is the unit the bit is keyed by. The two exceptions named are the whole set: the remaining conjunct, `typeof drv.aggregate === 'function'`, is true of any driver that can declare the bit usefully. The parity and collation sentences that follow are now scoped to the pushed-down call, where they are true by construction (same where compiler). S1: closed.
- **N1.** "`avg` / `min` / `max` over no values is `null`" matches the fold (values that are not null are kept, and none left answers `null`) and now covers the group a plain `groupBy` produces. N1: closed.
- Every other derived judgment of record 6897568297 rests on text this range does not touch, and holds on this head.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset is unchanged: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The PR body carries the same two lines. A lowered ratchet row in a repo script moves no package and no accept set, so the level and both declarations stay right.
- Check-runs on `d47493ba`, read at about 2026-11-15T16:46Z: 49 runs, 29 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed, 2 still running.
- Final and green on this head: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, the three scoped lint families and the `Lint & Repo Gates` roll-up; `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates`, `· consumer gates`, `· debt ledger` and the `TypeScript Type Check` roll-up; `Build Core`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `(2/8)`, `(3/8)` and the `Test Core` roll-up (three shards is what the planner scheduled); `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, and the first runs of `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size` and `Auto Label`. Every lint family that was still running when the earlier record was written has now reported green on the new head, the families the ratchet script's presence adds among them.
- Not final: a second `Check Changeset` and a second `PR-body guards` run, both started 16:45Z by the PR-body replacement. Their first runs on this same head are green; the reruns read the r2 body and are the seat's to see finish. The second `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` runs from that event completed as skipped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The range stays inside the claim's file surface: the claim names "ratchet rows only if they move", and the row moved at the reviewer's request.
- The PR body says `b87277b6` was authored at the contract-review tier like the first commit. As before, I cannot verify that from the inputs given; it is the seat's to hold with the transcript.
- The r2 body's size table and gate count agree with the tree: `filters.md` 9892 bytes, `aggregation.md` 9053 bytes, row `2473 / 2473`, row `2264 / 2357`. The table's caption still names head `a7754819` while its figures are this head's; prose face, the seat's.
- The body's NOT MEASURED line still says no pin was read for driver-memory's own `where`. Record 6897568297 named the pin (`memory-matcher-null-value-and-comparand.test.ts`, #13553). The body understates; nothing in the tree is affected.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md` (changed in the range). The callout is now true for every call shape (①), and it agrees with the Date-Bucketed Grouping section of the same file, which already teaches the fallback to in-memory bucketing. The clause costs 43 tokens against 136 of headroom; the file measures 2264 against its unchanged row of 2357. The HAVING sentence reads correctly with "no values". No other line of the file moved.

N4 (nit): the re-wrap left one line of the callout at 87 characters ("a column the object does not declare, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. On any other driver the") where the block wraps near 78. No effect on rendering, meaning or the token count; fix it the next time the file is touched.

`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` (in the diff, enforces the `hits` files). The row for `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` goes from 2482 to 2473 and no other row moves. Judged against the gate's own discipline: lowering is the direction the header calls always legitimate, the new value is pinned AT the measurement, and the arithmetic in the comment is right: the file is 9892 bytes on this head, 9892 / 4 is exactly 2473, headroom 0, which is where the file sat on main. The comment follows the form of the rows around it (what was paid, where each cut's home is, the byte arithmetic) and both homes it names are the ones record 6897568297 verified. The earlier comment block for the 2149 to 2482 raise is kept above it, so the row's history reads in order. The `aggregation.md` row is correctly left alone: that file grew inside existing headroom and a raise was neither needed nor made. The gate's self-test and the dispatch-gates family the script's presence derives are green in CI on this head (`Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`). N3: closed.

`skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` and `skills/objectstack-query/evals/filters-pagination-search.json` are unchanged since record 6897568297, and its judgments on them hold on this head.

domain:skills#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRxXmVQ41fqnaTPGAv

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`objectstack-query` 技能跟上 #33854 的语义改动。`filters.md` 写明空值或缺列在 `$gt/$gte/$lt/$lte/$between` 下不命中(度量 `filter`、`having`、内存 `where` 一致),`null` 作排序比较值被拒(`INVALID_FILTER`/400);`aggregation.md` 删掉「条件聚合一律走内存、没有驱动能编译」这句错话,改为:声明 `supports.aggregationFilter` 的驱动在聚合本身下推时在库里算,非 UTC 时区的日期分桶或驱动不原生支持的粒度整次走内存;评测加第 8 例;`filters.md` 的 token 棘轮行 2482→2473(只降)。+54/−22,changeset `@objectstack/skills: patch`。
- 为什么改:#33854 改了引擎行为,技能还在教旧说法,建应用的 agent 会照错话写聚合过滤。
- 风险与回滚:只改技能文字、一个评测用例和一行棘轮上限,不动运行时。回滚 = revert。
- 先看:`aggregation.md` 的条件聚合提示框(复审 S1 修的那一句),再看 `filters.md` 新的「空值与排序运算符」一节。
- 两分钟验证:对照 `packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` 的下推条件(`tzRequiresInMemory`、`allStructuredSupported`、`aggregationFilterNative`),看提示框说的两种例外是否就是全部。
- 需要你做的:受管面 Tier H。低风险技能臂不适用,因为 diff 含 `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`(复审 N3 要求把棘轮行降到实测值)。达档(CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)复审:首轮 6897568297 PASS(S1 should-fix),delta 6897881498 在本 head PASS、S1 已关。请批准并合并,或批准后由席位落地。
- 席位意见:可以合。

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT, held for the maintainer** · head `d47493babcaa8ba290719aa97dc1a419d3f5e1f4` · card #33868 · report 6897496261 · at-tier contract review 6897568297 (round 1, PASS with S1) + delta 6897881498 (PASS on this head, `S1: closed`, `N1: closed`, `N3: closed`) · read 2026-11-15T16:48Z.

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #33868`. `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md`, `rules/aggregation.md`, `evals/filters-pagination-search.json` (case 8), `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` (one row lowered to the measurement), changeset `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. **GOVERNED**, Tier H. `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Premise measured:** PR #33854 (merged `0ac112fc`) changed the null ordering semantics this PR teaches; the review checked every taught sentence against main's code.
- **Gates:** on this head, none failing. Lint (all families, PM dispatch-gates included), Type Check, Build Core, Test Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI are green. The PR-body guard and Check Changeset re-runs from the body edits are the only ones still finishing at this read. The red `Lint & Repo Gates` / `TypeScript Type Check` on `b87277b6` were lanes cancelled by the merge push, not failures of this diff. Dev: 63 derived, 63 exit 0, `--ran` reconciles.
- **Accepted deviations:** authoring by a subagent pinned to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` inside a lower-tier thread (declared before the work, recorded in the body). S1 wording "the driver does not bucket natively" in place of the review's suggestion, judged more exact by the delta. `$empty` left unnamed (option A, judged right). Nits N2 and N4 left as they are. The body's two stale prose lines were corrected by the seat.
- **Out of scope:** none filed.
- **Landing:** Tier H. The seat does not flip this PR ready or enqueue it. It needs the maintainer's merge, or an authorised APPROVED review after which the seat lands it.
